News.title: Haaland double sees off Porto as Man City win feisty Champions League clash
News.content:
Enzo Maresca takes charge of his first Champions League game in charge of Manchester City as they have travelled to Portugal to take on Porto at the Estadio do Dragao. These sides last met during the Champions League group stages during the 2020/21 season. Manchester City won 3-1 at home before the two sides drew 0-0 in this stadium.

Manchester City were busy late on in the transfer window, bringing in both Iliman Ndiaye and Enzo Fernandez as they spent nearly £200m on deadline day alone. They come into tonight’s game off the back of three straight Premier League victories to kick off the Maresca era. Maresca has limited Champions League experience as a manager, which came with Chelsea last season. Manchester City have won their opening game of a Champions League campaign in six of the last seven seasons but this will be the first time since 2015/16 that Manchester City embark on a Champions League campaign without Pep Guardiola at the helm.

“It is a hard place to come [Porto],” said Maresca. “They have started really well. In the last 14/15 games in Europe they lost just one, that shows a difficult place to come, but we will try our best and try to win the game. It is a very, very good team. They have different players, but in terms of the team it is very clear in the way they play. They are aggressive without the ball and on the ball, they have a clear style. But we will try our best and try to win the game. The ambition is the same; try to be ourselves and to win games and then we will see.”

Porto, managed by Francesco Farioli, have won every league game so far this season and already sit four points clear at the summit of Liga Portugal. Farioli takes charge of his first game as a manger in the Champions League and the club make their return to the elite European competition after two seasons away.

“We are going to face one of the big favourites to win the competition,” Farioli said. “It will be a game that will demand that we be at our best, and we know that whenever we step onto the Dragão pitch, something special can happen. I am happy to be in the Champions League for the first time at 37 years old. This will be my first game, but we approach every game with the same attention to detail and the same focus. It is easy for the players to be motivated tomorrow [tonight]. But the key will be our strategy and our ability to execute it, individually and collectively.”

Porto were in the Europa League last season, making it to the quarter-finals, where they were knocked out by Nottingham Forest 2-1 on aggregate. The omens would not appear to be on Porto’s side tonight; they have only won two of their last 16 games against English opposition in major European competition.

Team news from Portugal to follow shortly.

News.title: Newcastle scrape past Millwall to extend Jaissle’s unbeaten start
News.content:
Joe Willock’s deft finish ensured Newcastle United survived a tough test against Millwall to keep their excellent run in the Carabao Cup intact.

This competition had been fruitful for Newcastle under former manager Eddie Howe and although this match was hard work – as well as hard to watch at times – his successor Matthias Jaissle guided them through a difficult trip to south-east London.

He called it “job done,” and that was pretty much all it was. “We needed patience on one hand, but also to be passionate and tough. We had the chance [to score] and took it,” he said.

Newcastle have reached the semi-finals of this competition three times in the last four years, but struggled to get any sort of tempo going against their Championship opponents.

You could argue the winning goal came against the run of play late in the second half, moments after Millwall substitute Taïryk Arconte had smashed a low shot against the post.

News.title: Villa end goal drought to finally give Emery’s new era lift-off
News.content:
Unai Emery is building Aston Villa 2.0 and this was a night when his new kids on the block produced clear signs of lift-off for the next chapter.

Emery always springs into life on European nights and his reconstructed team secured their first win and goals of the season to leave Villa’s 1,700 fans singing in the rain.

Ten summer signings have arrived during a summer of upheaval which included plenty of high-profile departures after the club’s Europa League triumph in May.

Yet this was an evening that will have further energised Emery on his return to the Champions League.

Nicolas Jackson, Zion Suzuki and João Gomes embody this new Villa team and all stood out here in Bruges.

Record £65m signing Jackson’s fine individual goal proved to be the winner to settle a chaotic, absorbing contest with the Belgian Pro League champions.

News.title: Bird flu threatens French foie gras amid new duck cull
News.content:
The latest cull - like previous ones - was undertaken to protect both animal and human health.

Ducks are killed to stop the spread of the disease between farms, as well as to protect the health of farmers and minimise the risk of the virus mutating.

It is thought foie gras itself does not pose a risk to human health, even if it came from a bird-flu-infected duck, because it is almost always heat-treated before it is sold, which effectively destroys the virus, according to Public Health France.

“The consumption of meat, foie gras and eggs – and more generally of any food product based on poultry – presents no risk to humans,” said a spokesman for the Maine-et-Loire prefecture.

Veterinary experts say ducks are especially problematic regarding H5N1 because they can carry the virus without showing symptoms and have been described as the Chevaux de Troie or “Trojan horses” of bird flu.

It is unclear how the birds in the latest outbreak, located on a farm in Longué-Jumelles, contracted the virus, although it is typically spread by wild birds which shed the virus through their droppings.

It is for this reason that British poultry were forced into lockdown or “flockdown” from late October to April of this year.

This included so-called “free-range” birds, which, as the Telegraph reported in November continued to be described as free-range despite never seeing the light of day under a dispensation given by the Department for Environment, Food, and Rural Affairs (DEFRA).

Ducks reared for foie gras typically spend the first 90 days of their lives being reared in their tens of thousands in barns with very little access to natural light.

Animal rights campaigners say most never see water.

They then are put through a rigorous 12-16 day “fattening up” period where they are force-fed through a tube to significantly enlarge their livers, before being slaughtered.

While France introduced a vaccination programme to protect its duck population from bird flu in 2023, the jabs do not entirely stop the virus from getting into a flock.

Data collected by the French Agency for Food, Environmental and Occupational Health & Safety suggested that between 50 and 55 per cent of the country’s ducks are unvaccinated at any given time, due to a 20-day gap between the first and second dose of the vaccine and waning immunity over time.

The ducks subject to the latest bird-flu cull in Western France had received their first dose of the H5N1 vaccine, but not the second, meaning they were not fully protected, according to the disease monitoring firm Airfinity.

The threat to France’s £2 billion foie gras industry comes amid increasing global competition.

Once the dominant producer, it is now being challenged by China, which has rapidly scaled up its output of the delicacy and now accounts for 45 per cent of global production.

A tin of Chinese foie gras costs roughly £3.70, while a typical tin of French foie gras made from duck liver costs between £10 and £15. French foie gras produced from Geese costs anywhere between £70 and £150.

China is also said to operate a more rigorous poultry vaccination programme, according to an analysis by DEFRA.

It applies to all farmed birds in the country, which has managed to keep outbreaks of bird flu on farms relatively low compared with European levels.

The H5N1 avian flu pandemic has now been running for six years and has decimated flocks of farmed chickens and turkeys across the globe.

In the UK alone, more than five million farmed birds have been culled since 2021, costing an estimated £48 million in farmers’ compensation alone.

Last week, the virus was detected on a mink farm in the US state of Utah.

Minks in captivity have previously been described as pandemic “time bombs”. The size and density of fur farms – where thousands of the animals are crammed together in tight proximity – give invading viruses a perfect environment in which to mutate.

The virus has also done huge damage to wild birds and other animals. In South America alone, more than 600,000 wild seabirds have died since 2022.

Dozens of other mammals have been infected and died across the globe, including foxes, otters, sea lions, bears, and seals.

In June, the virus was found in Australia for the first time – the last continent on earth to record a case – and the government has since launched a vaccination programme to protect the country’s rare species, including birds like orange-bellied parrots and black cockatoos.

Scientists have long warned that if H5N1 gains the mutations necessary to spread between people, it could trigger a human-pandemic, something that would be of “enormous concern”, according to the World Health Organization (WHO), given the virus’s 50 per cent case fatality rate.

News.title: The Chancellor’s speech, as it happened
News.content:
John Healey failed to rule out tax rises at next month’s Budget in his first major speech as Chancellor.

Mr Healey also sought to blame Liz Truss and her mini-Budget in 2022 for the high borrowing costs being paid by the Treasury.

During a speech in Coventry, the Chancellor said he would be “honest” about the need to control public spending during his time in Number 11.

He was speaking days after the cost of government borrowing hit its highest level since 2007.

It was also overshadowed by Jaguar Land Rover announcing plans to cut 4,000 jobs in the face of “intense competition and ongoing geopolitical uncertainty”.

Read our report on the Chancellor’s speech.

News.title: Maitland-Niles’ last-gasp debut goal salvages Everton’s miserable week
News.content:
At the final whistle, the first song the stadium DJ played was Spirit of the Blues and how those relieved Evertonians lapped it up after a week of angst.

Their team had been on the precipice of a defeat that would have exacerbated all the frustrations that bubbled away following the chaotic conclusion to the transfer window. Indeed, it was 10 seconds over the allotted five minutes of added time when the ball fell to Ainsley Maitland-Niles.

It had been three years since the former Arsenal full-back had played in the Premier League – his last goal in England was on October 30, 2019, in an EFL Cup tie with Liverpool at Anfield that ended 5-5 – and he would not have joined Everton if their attempt to sign Kenny Tete from Fulham had not failed.

But here he was 30 yards from goal, with no need to break his stride as Manchester United’s backtracking defenders presented him with an invitation to shoot. So that’s what he did. With one perfectly timed swish of his right foot, an unlikely hero transformed the mood of a club.

News.title: Arsenal teach Chelsea a lesson in how to be champions
News.content:
This is how champions are supposed to play and, although the Arsenal home support have not seen a team defend their place at the apex of English league football for two decades, they knew it when they saw it.

The chase was on for Mikel Arteta’s team within two minutes when Morgan Rogers, the man who might have moved to Arsenal this summer, put his new club Chelsea in the lead. So unfolded a thrilling 100 minutes of Premier League competition. Arsenal were the better team in terms of ambition and attack even if one could not discount Chelsea until the very last moment.

Others might have crumbled. That Chelsea did not will give Xabi Alonso hope for a team that did not feature the injured Moisés Caicedo and is now without the departed Enzo Fernández. Yet he will also recognise that his childhood friend from San Sebastián in the other dugout has created a side that treated the game, and their place in it, with an urgency that looks different. The first two minutes might have been ragged for Arsenal but after that they did not let the game happen to them.

Sports.title: Man Utd REJECTED chance to sign Kylian Mbappe after Ryan Giggs scouting mission
Sports.content:
Ryan Giggs has revealed how Manchester United once turned down the chance to sign Kylian Mbappe.

Giggs was working on the coaching staff at United back in 2015 when a random stranger recommended his club take a look at Mbappe, who was at Monaco at the time. Giggs, appearing on 'Rio Ferdinand Presents: The Debrief', went to watch the striker in action before recommending United do the same.

Which United's scouting team did - before deciding he wouldn't be good enough for them. Mbappe has gone on to become a footballing superstar, having won the World Cup with France before scoring a hat-trick in a second final.

Mbappe joined Paris Saint Germain in 2018 for £162m - the second most expensive signing in football history. He won the Golden Boot at this summer's World Cup, while becoming the all-time leading scorer in the tournament's history.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Now Giggs has spoken about how Mbappe slipped through United's grasp - in what might just be one of the biggest mistakes the English giants have ever made.

Giggs said: "So, I’m in the south of France. I've been for a walk in the local village and I'm walking back to the hotel. And I can feel someone, you know, when you feel someone like following you. I get to the hotel and then all of a sudden I can feel someone coming up to me.

"This guy is called Lionel. He comes up to me and says, 'hi, I’m Lionel. I just wanted to just say hello. I'm a big United fan and big fan of yours.

‌



'But I watch a lot of youth football in France, and you have to look at this player. He's called Kylian Mbappé. He's at Monaco and I think he's a player for Manchester United.

View 2 Images Ryan Giggs has revealed he suggested Kylian Mbappe to Real Madrid (Image: Getty Images)

"A few weeks later, he emailed me all the details. So me and Albert, he was another assistant at United at the time, I've told him about this thing.

"We go to a few youth games with Monaco and we've seen him (Mbappe) and we were just like, 'wow, what is this?' You can see players and they can be special, but he did look exceptional, obviously.

‌



"We told the (United) scouting team. They went to watch him. Someone in France went to watch him and he was actually playing PSG.

"Monaco were playing PSG. So they went to Paris to watch him. Anyway, I think a few weeks later, I said to this guy, 'how did it go?' He went, 'yeah, they weren't too sure about him, so we just left it'. And that was it."

Sports.title: Erling Haaland delivers again to help Man City survive Porto scare - 5 talking points
Sports.content:
Erling Haaland delivers again to help Man City survive Porto scare - 5 talking points

PORTO 0-2 MAN CITY: A brace from Erling Haaland decided the game for Manchester City once again, as they took maximum points from their awkward Champions League opener

View 5 Images Manchester City are up and running in the Champions League (Image: PATRICIA DE MELO MOREIRA/AFP via Getty Images)

Manchester City got their Champions League campaign off to a winning start with a hard-fought 2-0 victory over Porto. Erling Haaland netted both goals in Portugal to make it five for the season, having also decided Saturday's win against Coventry.

‌



City returned to the scene of their Champions League final defeat to Chelsea in 2021 with a new man in the dugout. Enzo Maresca didn't have easy time watching his team toil in the the pouring rain, but they earned their fourth successive win under him.

They were left frustrated in the first half, much thanks to the heroics of Diogo Costa. The Porto goalkeeper made a string of impressive saves, including two from Haaland to keep the Premier League giants at bay.

But it didn't take long for City to break through at the start of the second period - and third time was a charm for Haaland, whose header hit the post before nestling in the back of the net. It was then backs to the wall until full-time, as Porto pushed for an equaliser before City's goalscorer supreme struck again.

Here are five talking points from the Estadio do Dragao.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

1. Haaland starts despite Maresca hint

Erling Haaland's daddy issues was the main talking point from Enzo Maresca's pre-match press conference on Monday. The City boss explained how Haaland, now bearing the responsibilities of being a father, will need to be rested at some point this season following a busy 2025-26 campaign which ended in a deep run at the World Cup with Norway, who made it to the quarter-finals.

With deadline-day arrival Iliman Ndiaye now at his disposal, would Maresca rotate his striker? No. The 26-year-old was named in the starting XI alongside £86million signing Ayyoub Bouaddi, who was handed his full debut in midfield next to Enzo Fernandez after a cameo against Coventry.

Will Man City win the Champions League? Give us your prediction in the comments section.

View 5 Images Erling Haaland isn't being rested yet (Image: PATRICIA DE MELO MOREIRA/AFP via Getty Images)

2. VAR looks past Guehi incident

With the first half meandering to a close, City were flexing their muscles and causing Porto some discomfort. Marc Guehi did that quite literally when challenging Gabri Veiga for a bouncing ball, drawing blood from the Porto star's head.

Guehi's arm wasn't outstretched but the hosts became incensed after watching replays of the incident on the touchline. Francesco Farioli suggested that the City centre-back had elbowed his midfielder.

Veiga received treatment for a good few minutes, giving VAR plenty of time to assess the collision. But nothing was given, allowing referee Szymon Marciniak to signal for the restart without going to the monitor.

But when Marciniak blew his whistle for half-time, he was greeted by deafening whistles from the home crowd. The Polish official was also swarmed by Porto players as he attempted to get down the tunnel.

View 5 Images Gabriel Veiga took a heavy blow from Marc Guehi (Image: Clive Brunskill/Getty Images)

3. Who else but Haaland?

Need someone to break the deadlock? Call Erling Haaland.

The Norwegian has now scored the first goal in City's last three games. This time he easily beat Jakub Kiwior in the air and headed Fernandez's cross back the way it came, leaving Costa wrong-footed.

It seemed to take an age for the ball to go in, but there was relief when it eventually did. The header marked Haaland's 58th Champions League goal - in just 59 games - taking him clear of Bayern Munich legend Thomas Muller.

View 5 Images Erling Haaland rose highest to give Manchester City the lead (Image: Miguel RIOPA/AFP via Getty Images)

4. No messing from Maresca

After going 1-0 up, City suddenly became vulnerable and sloppiness seeped - or flooded more accurately - into their performance. Their tendency to give possession cheaply away left Maresca furious in his technical area and he made a double substitution shortly after a poor passage of play.

Rayan Cherki, twice the source of his manager's frustration, came off alongside Antoine Semenyo, who had a difficult night. Ndiaye and Elliot Anderson were their replacements as Porto smelled blood.

View 5 Images Enzo Maresca saw the danger coming (Image: PATRICIA DE MELO MOREIRA/AFP via Getty Images)

5. Dodgy Donnarumma

Although Maresca wasn't happy with his outfielders, it was his goalkeeper who nearly made two fatal mistakes. Gianluigi Donnarumma flattened Pepe in the 49th minute, and while the offside flag saved him from giving away a penalty, he was still booked for his challenge.

Shortly after the hour mark, Donnarumma misjudged a pass which was played back to him and got chased down by William Gomes as he hurriedly attempted to clear his lines. Luckily for the Italian, his blocked clearance flew back towards goal but whizzed past the post.

Porto never properly tested the City No.1 in the closing stages, getting caught offside on numerous occasions despite their pace. And when Haaland made it 2-0 with a cool finish inside the penalty area, Maresca could breathe a sigh of relief after two narrow victories in four days ahead of the Manchester derby at Old Trafford this Sunday.

Sports.title: Wayne Rooney issues Michael Carrick sack warning and says Bruno Fernandes won't be happy
Sports.content:
Wayne Rooney issues Michael Carrick sack warning and says Bruno Fernandes won't be happy

Manchester United have only managed to win one of their opening three Premier League matches, a far cry from the red-hot form which they enjoyed under Michael Carrick last season

View 2 Images Wayne Rooney fears for Michael Carrick (Image: The Overlap)

Wayne Rooney has warned Michael Carrick that he needs results now and can't wait for another transfer window to fix Manchester United's problems. The Red Devils legend also criticised United's summer business which saw them fail in their search to bolster their defence.

‌



Carrick's side have mustered just four points from their first three games of the Premier League season, conceding a worrying six goals in the process. United began the campaign with a shock 2-0 loss away to newly promoted Hull before thrashing Ipswich 5-2 at Old Trafford in their second outing.

‌



But off the back of Sunday's late 2-2 draw with Everton, in which the Red Devils threw away the lead twice, Rooney is concerned for his ex-team-mate. "If you're manager of Manchester United you know the pressure which comes with the job and the time now you're not getting much time in the job," the former striker explained on the Stick to United podcast.

‌



"You have to push as hard as you can even harder to get players in because you know you don't want to be sitting here in six months, 12 months' time, saying 'You know what? I should have'.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"Do we want to win the Champions League? Of course we do. But in terms of this process we're going through to try and get back to that, we're going to have to accept we're not quite at that level yet. Arsenal have been through this process over the last five years with [Mikel] Arteta and you've seen the progress each year."

Rooney went on to say: "I know Michael's come out and said he's happy with the players they've got in. I don't think any manager's happy.

"He's going to have to come out and say the right things. Of course… every manager does that. But he hasn't got time to wait for next year. He can't sit there and go 'Well, you know what? I'll wait till next year,' then I'll have my defence sorted. You're getting more and more American owners who want success straight away."

‌



Is Michael Carrick the right man for Manchester United? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Michael Carrick needs to find a solution quickly (Image: Lewis Storey - Danehouse/Getty Images)

Rooney also claimed that United captain Bruno Fernandes won't be happy with the club's decision to only sign three midfielders and a No.2 goalkeeper in the summer window. "There is nothing in there which is saying to me now these players are going to take Man United to the next level," he continued.

‌



"I love Bruno. I think he's brilliant. He must be thinking 'Right, please bring me some help. I'm doing everything I can. Help me'. And I don't think the club have done that with the signings.

"You're not sitting there saying you've got these four players we should be winning the Premier League. You're sitting there saying these players need more help than what they've been getting.

Rooney added: "We're Man United. We've won so many Premier Leagues, Champions Leagues, whatever. The fans will still be thinking that's what we want. But, realistically, they're not there."

Sports.title: One week after the transfer window closes, Man Utd remind fans what they're really about
Sports.content:
One week after the transfer window closes, Man Utd remind fans what they're really about

Manchester United needed a new defender, but have got a shirt sleeve sponsor instead, reminding supporters what the priorities of the club's owners still are

View 2 Images Manchester United co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe (Image: Valery HACHE/AFP via Getty Images)

It has come a week after the transfer window slammed shut. So the news will mean little or nothing to long-suffering Manchester United supporters.

‌



But the club HAS made a signing.

‌



Not the left back the team continues to cry out for, or a central defender to ease the burden on Harry Maguire and Lisandro Martinez as United head back into the demands of Champions League football. Instead, United have landed a new shirt sleeve sponsor. The most lucrative one in the club's history, no less. The multi-million pound agreement is with financial tech giants SumUp.

‌



It follows in the footsteps of the record-breaking training kit sponsorship deal with 'Betway', said to be worth £20m-a-year.

SumUp's chief commercial officer and UK chief executive Luke Griffiths said: "Manchester United is one of the most iconic and followed clubs in the world, with a fanbase that continues to grow across generations and borders.

"That extraordinary reach and passion make this partnership a natural fit for SumUp. Football is about the moments people share. Watching the match with friends, travelling to see the team, wearing the shirt with pride and celebrating together, wherever you are. From fans using SumUp Personal Account to manage and spend their money simply, to the businesses that help make matchdays special, SumUp is part of the everyday moments that bring people together."

‌



Paul Ince recalls horrifying Glenn Hoddle incident as fans urged to back heart campaign READ MORE :

Man Utd strike deal to land Liverpool wonderkid in major transfer coup READ MORE :

View 2 Images The Glazers continue milk United like the cash cow it has served to be (Image: PA)

United might still be able to generate huge incomes from commercial deals, but it also remains a club created by the poor, and stolen by the rich.

Success on and off the pitch is supposed to go hand-in-hand. But where United are concerned, nothing could be further from the truth, because the fallen giants have not won a title since 2013, or conquered Europe since 2008. They haven't even come close.

‌



Along with the continued grip of the Glazer ownership, this is what infuriates supporters the most.

And while it is ever thus, the red half of Manchester will remain one very much divided - as opposed to United.

Sports.title: Scott McTominay health update as Napoli issue statement following heart surgery
Sports.content:
Scott McTominay health update as Napoli issue statement following heart surgery

Scott McTominay went under the knife after he was diagnosed with a mild benign arrhythmia - an irregular heart rhythm - and Napoli have provided an update following the procedure

View 2 Images Scott McTominay had the surgery in Manchester (Image: Ivan Romano/Getty Images)

Scott McTominay has undergone successful surgery to correct a minor heart issue, Napoli have confirmed. The former Manchester United star was recently diagnosed with a mild benign arrhythmia, an irregular heart rhythm which is deemed non-serious but required a procedure.

McTominay, 29, went under the knife in Manchester on Tuesday and Napoli say that the surgery was a 'complete success'. The Serie A side added that their midfielder is expected to return to action following the upcoming international break.

"On Tuesday morning, Scott McTominay underwent an ablation procedure at Spire Manchester Hospital," Napoli said in a statement. "The operation was a complete success. McTominay will rest for two weeks and then resume training."

‌



The Scotland international has also played down the seriousness of the issue, saying at a recent awards ceremony: "I'm fine, the procedure was something I'd planned to do with the club for quite a while."

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

McTominay's procedure forced him to miss Napoli's 3-2 defeat away to Inter Milan last Saturday. He'll be unavailable for a further three Napoli matches, including their Champions League opener at home to Arsenal on Wednesday.

Max Allegri will hope to have McTominay available when his side host Frosinone on October 10 in their first game after the international break. Napoli have lost two of their opening three Serie A fixtures leaving them 12th in the table and six points off the top.

Scotland will also have to manage without McTominay for the start of new boss Sebastien Pocognoli's reign. Following their disappointing World Cup exit, Scotland will look to rebuild across four Nations League matches which take place between September 26 and October 6.

‌



View 2 Images Scott McTominay is due to return in October (Image: Mairo Cinquetti/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

McTominay's long-term future in Naples has also been a talking point this week. Contracted until 2028, there's uncertainty over whether he'll sign a new deal.

He signed for Napoli under Antonio Conte two years ago in a deal worth £25.7million, winning the Italian title in his first season and being named Serie A Player of the Season. Napoli sporting director Giovanni Manna addressed the uncertainty surrounding the 29-year-old in an interview with DAZN.

‌



"Scott said he doesn't know if he'll renew at this time," Manna explained. "He has a two-year contract, we want to do it, and he wants to do it, too. It's not always easy to make things coincide, but we're trying."

McTominay was sold by United in the summer of 2024 after spending more than two decades with the Red Devils. He made 255 first-team appearances, winning the FA Cup and Carabao Cup.

Sports.title: Arsenal escape UEFA fine after being forced to cancel Champions League press conference
Sports.content:
Arsenal escape UEFA fine after being forced to cancel Champions League press conference

Arsenal face Napoli in their first match of the 2026-27 Champions League campaign, but their preparation has got off to an unideal start

View 3 Images Arsenal begin their Champions League campaign tomorrow (Image: 2026 Getty Images)

Arsenal have escaped a UEFA for missing the pre-match press conference for their opening Champions League clash against Napoli. The Gunners have experienced severe travel chaos on their way to Naples.

‌



Like hundreds, if not thousands, of travellers, the north Londoners plans have been impacted by flight delays. It's understood a technical problem has been affecting air traffic control systems at airports around the UK.

‌



As a result of the delays, the Gunners will not arrive in Naples in time for their scheduled pre-match press conference. Teams who do not fulfil their media obligations are often punished with a fine by UEFA.

‌



FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Many sides often receive a financial penalty if their conference is delayed by at least an hour. However, UEFA rules do state pre-match plans can be changed if circumstances beyond their control force them to do so.

Their official rules state: "Clubs may only change their MD-1 plans on account of force majeure and with the agreement of UEFA."

‌



The technical issue impacting the airports in London is out of the Gunners control, meaning they will not be penalised by European football's governing body. Mikel Arteta's side typically travel to European matches via Luton airport, which has been impacted by the technical error.

Last season, Liverpool found themselves in a similar scenario when their travel plans were disrupted. Before their group-stage clash against Eintracht Frankfurt, a flight delay caused by "technical issues with the aircraft" resulted in the Merseysiders arriving in Germany later than expected.

‌



View 3 Images Arsenal trained at their London Colney training base this morning (Image: 2026 The Arsenal Football Club Plc)

Despite the fact they had to miss their conference, they were not fined. While it impacted their media obligations, it did not stop Liverpool from beating Eintracht convincingly.

They came from behind to overcome the Bundesliga side 5-1, with Hugo Ekitike, Virgil van Dijk, Ibrahima Konate, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai all finding the net. Arsenal will certainly be hoping for a similar result when they face Massimiliano Allegri's side in Naples.

‌



View 3 Images Arsenal were left devastated in last season's final (Image: 2026 Marc Atkins)

They got all the way to the final in last season's campaign, which saw them agonisingly lose on penalties to Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League. Arteta's side were unstoppable in the group phase last season.

They won all eight of their matches, scoring 23 goals and only conceding four. Their campaign begins with a meeting with Napoli, before clashes with Lille, Bayern Munich, Slavia Prague, Borussia Dortmund, Real Madrid, Real Betis and Sabah follow.

Sports.title: Bowen at the double as West Ham climb top of the Championship
Sports.content:
Captain Jarrod Bowen scored twice as West Ham's 3-2 win over Bolton took them top of the Sky Bet Championship on goal difference and earned a first ever win at the Toughsheet Community Stadium.

The England international opened the scoring after 13 minutes and earned last season's Premier League outfit a first win in Bolton for 31 years with his second 13 minutes from time.

In between, Wanderers, beaten for a fourth successive outing, equalised through midfielder Ethan Erhahon's maiden goal for the Trotters.

Image: Jarrod Bowen's double helped West Ham to a dramatic victory

And they looked on course for a ninth successive league victory over the Hammers when Ruben Rodrigues converted a 27th-minute penalty.

Instead, Konstantinos Mavropanos levelled with a 31st-minute header and Bowen completed the comeback.

It came as no surprise when Bowen gave West Ham the lead, lofting a left-foot shot high into the net after Gavin Bazunu blocked a close-range Pablo effort.

The Hammers' advantage lasted just five minutes before ex-Lincoln midfielder Erhahon equalised with a rasping left-foot strike that hit Mavropanos on its way beyond Mads Hermansen.

Looking for their first second-tier success since the opening day of the campaign, Bolton hit the front after 27 minutes.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jarrod Bowen opens the scoring at Bolton as visitors West Ham go 1-0 in front.

Kyle Walker-Peters was already struggling to contain winger Kyliane Dong, when he felled the Augsburg loanee.

Rodrigues - who netted twice in Bolton's League One play-off final win last May, including a penalty - sent Hermansen the wrong way from the spot.

Now it was West Ham's turn to fashion a swift riposte. Arne Engels guided a free-kick to the far post where Mavropanos climbed highest to head in an equaliser.

The Greek centre-back almost reprised his goal soon after but from Bowen's inswinging corner, debutant Bazunu clawed the ball from under his crossbar.

Bolton, though, finished the half on top with the lively Dong shooting wide and Sam Dalby denied by Hermansen's stoppage-time save.

The action was less frenetic in the second half with West Ham more in control.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jarrod Bowen scored his second goal of the game as West Ham United reclaimed the lead against Bolton Wanderers.

Substitute Manor Solomon should have done better with a chance provided by Bowen while another replacement, Joel Piroe, blazed high into the away fans with only Bazunu to beat.

Bowen finally squeezed a close-range shot into the net despite Bazunu's desperate attempt to stop the ball trickling over the line.

And he should have completed a last-minute hat-trick but Wales international Josh Sheehan chased back to block the shot.

Sports.title: Willock grabs late goal as Newcastle edge Millwall
Sports.content:
Joe Willock's late goal sent a relieved Newcastle into the fourth round of the Carabao Cup as the Premier League side scraped to a 1-0 victory at Sky Bet Championship outfit Millwall.

Just before going ahead, the Magpies had been given a fright when a shot from Tairyk Arconte hit a post, with the hosts at that point threatening to upset the competition's winners of two seasons ago.

The Lions brought on 15-year-old midfielder Regan Anderson, who became Millwall's second youngest player, in the time that remained, but Newcastle held firm in what was a hard-fought tie.

Jacob Murphy bent a shot harmlessly over in the early exchanges in what was the first meeting between the two teams since 1993.

The first time Millwall's debutant goalkeeper Filip Marschall was called into action was in the 15th minute when he parried Willock's strike into the air, with the ball dropping to left-back Elkan Baggott rather than the lurking Yoane Wissa.

The visitors dominated the early proceedings and came close again when Sven Botman headed Murphy's corner narrowly over at the far post.

A rare foray out of their own half by the hosts led to their first half-chance as Lyndon Dykes' hooked effort from Baggott's cross was gathered easily by Lukas Hornicek.

The Lions were providing a threat from set-pieces, with a good delivery from a free-kick by Camiel Neghli being met by a flying header from Caleb Taylor that went just wide.

Newcastle then almost had a stroke of luck at the other end as Fabian Schar's long-range effort took a big deflection and ruffled the side-netting, with Marschall stranded.

It remained deadlocked at the break and Millwall began the second half brightly with Jenson Metcalfe smashing a long-range effort just over within two minutes of the restart.

A Metcalfe free-kick then led to another warning for the away side as a header from Lions captain Jake Cooper drifted wide.

The Magpies had struggled to impose themselves since half-time, although Harvey Barnes had just their second shot on target after 65 minutes when his tame effort was easily saved by Marschall.

Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle sent on Anthony Elanga and deadline day signing Matias Fernandez-Pardo in an effort to finally force a breakthrough, but the Millwall centre-back pairing of Cooper and Caleb Taylor were repelling everything coming their way.

Millwall substitute Arconte was the closest to opening the scoring in the 79th minute when he got away from Tino Livramento before his shot came back off the near post.

Having survived that scare, the visitors snatched victory with nine minutes left when Lewis Hall's ball across the six-yard box was flicked in by Willock.

Image: Lewis Hall was quiick to praise new boss Matthias Jaissle

Hall hails Jaissle for lifting Newcastle negativity after cup win

Newcastle defender Lewis Hall speaking to Sky Sports:

"There was a lot of negativity before everything happened and as soon as the gaffer came in, he's been top, as well as all of the coaching staff.

"The way he's got us playing is amazing and I can speak on behalf of everyone - we're really enjoying playing under him.

"We knew it was going to be tough. Whenever you come away in the cup, anything can happen, so we're really proud of the win and to keep a clean sheet as well."

Willock: The Carabao Cup is important for us

Newcastle midfielder Joe Willock speaking to Sky Sports:

"We had a lot of chances in the first half, but we said at half-time that we needed to take our chances. Thankfully, in the second half we did, we got a goal and won the game.

"We won this competition before so it's very important to us. We've got a new coach and a lot of new players and we wanted to start the season well.

"I feel like we started it really well. We need to continue, and this was a big game in keeping that momentum."

Image: Matthias Jaissle remains unbeaten as Newcastle boss

Jaissle: It was all about patience

Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle speaking to Sky Sports:

"We're really happy. Job done. It's never going to be easy here at Millwall in a cup match, so we knew about that challenge and we faced it.

"It was about patience, but also being passionate, being tough, collecting the second balls and being efficient in front of their goal. We used the chance and therefore I'm really proud.

"We matched the physical challenge quite well and made a step in the right direction compared to the first half against Bournemouth. We brought the fundamentals onto the pitch, therefore I'm pleased.

"Joe [Willock] is doing an excellent job. Since we joined, already in pre-season, you saw that there is potential.

"I'm really happy with the start so far. I think we show unity on the pitch and off the pitch already after such a short amount of time. But again, we are realistic. We're happy, we're grateful for that start and now the focus is already towards Leeds.

"I love it [English football]. Honestly, I love it. Coming out for an evening match and knowing that atmosphere is something you dream about. It's a privilege."

Sports.title: Haaland scores twice in win over Porto but Man City struggle to impress
Sports.content:
Erling Haaland's double earned Manchester City a 2-0 win at FC Porto - but it was another game where Enzo Maresca's side won but struggled to convince.

City's main man up front was surprisingly wasteful in the first half, seeing two glorious chances in the area saved by Diogo Costa as well as heading another good chance over the bar.

Porto's goalkeeper was in inspired form in the opening 45 minutes, also saving well from Rayan Cherki from the rebound of one of Haaland's chances.

But Haaland took just two minutes of the second period to make amends, barging Jakub Kiwior aside to nod an Enzo Fernandez cross in off the post.

But City then took their foot off the gas as the Portuguese champions started to grow in confidence. Porto failed to produce a shot on target but Alan Varela curled just wide of the far post from the edge of the box in a warning shot.

Image: Haaland scored twice in the second half

Then Gianluigi Donnarumma was nearly caught in possession by Porto forward William Gomes, with the City goalkeeper lucky to see the ball run away to safety. City did find a way to seal the result, however, as Haaland tucked home Rayan Ait-Nouri's cutback in stoppage time.

Erling's on Sergio's level! Erling Haaland scored his 36th UEFA Champions League goal for Manchester City, equalling Sergio Agüero as joint-most for the Citizens in the competition.

Despite another game this season where City have won but struggled to impress at the same time, Maresca failed to win away of his three away Champions League ties as Chelsea boss last term.

He will see a winning start to this campaign as a positive - especially as City have become the first team to beat Porto at the Estadio do Dragao this calendar year.

But improvement is needed ahead of Sunday's Manchester derby at Old Trafford, live on Sky Sports.

Manchester United

Manchester City Sunday 13th September 4:00pm Kick off 4:30pm

The key moments from Estadio do Dragao

16: SAVE! Antoine Semenyo starts the game brightly and curls an early effort into Diogo Costa's gloves.

21: BIG CHANCE FOR HAALAND! Semenyo feeds Phil Foden who clips a cross into the box for Haaland - who is denied by a smart glove from Costa.

27: BIG MISS! Haaland heads over another good chance via a cross from the left, this time from Semenyo.

29: BIG SAVE! Foden goes on a mazy run in and around the penalty area and forces another save from Costa.

31: DOUBLE SAVE! A man possessed! Costa denies Haaland's low drive from inside the box, then gets up to stop Rayan Cherki at the rebound.

42: OUCH! Marc Guehi catches Gabri Veiga with his arm which causes a lot of blood. With Porto calling for a red card for a violent elbow, the Man City defender avoids punishment. It was more accidental rather than malicious.

47: GOAL! Haaland takes just two minutes to rectify his wasteful first half by nodding a header in off the post from Enzo Fernandez's cross.

49: NO PENALTY! City goalkeeper Donnarumma clatters into Porto winger Pepe in the box… but the offside flag goes up against the forward.

57: SO CLOSE! Porto midfielder Alan Varela gets a chance to shoot and curls just wide of the far post. That was Porto's first shot of the game.

66: NERVY! Donnarumma is nearly caught in possession by Porto forward Gomes, but the ball runs behind for a goal kick.

85: JUST WIDE! City substitute Ait-Nouri has the chance to seal the result but steers a shot wide of goal from a good area.

90+1: GOAL! Haaland seals the result by slotting home Ait-Nouri's cutback after he did well to get to the byline.

Should Maresca be happy about Man City's performance?

Image: Erling Haaland gave Man City a win but they weren't convincing

Man City striker Erling Haaland to Amazon Prime:

"I hope so, we win away in a difficult game. Look at this atmosphere, it was unreal at times. So I hope [yes].

"Amazing game against the champions of Portugal. We knew it was going to be a difficult fight, man against man. They're a top team, impressive, all of them. They play amazing football.

"Well done to them. But with all the pressure, we have to deliver on the biggest stage. That's what we did tonight.

"Honestly we controlled the whole first half. Of course, it's a bit uncomfortable when they come high. But we created a lot of chances. I could have easily had a few more goals.

"But second half we scored and they managed to push us for a good 25 minutes. We managed to hold through and finish the game.

"These are the games we have to win. We had a great start to the season and in the Champions League, you have to win games. If not, you get all the pressure. You never know what's going to happen.

"We have to learn. Enzo has to demand a lot from us and each other. At Manchester City, you have to win games and win trophies, that's what we have to do."

And here's Maresca's verdict - he's happy!

Man City head coach Enzo Maresca to Amazon Prime:

"We could have scored more goals, especially in the first half. But overall we deserved to win the game. We created enough chances to win the game, we didn't concede a lot.

"It's normal to come here and concede some noises so overall I'm happy with the performance.

"If you think you're going to come here in this stadium and just play and not concede anything, it's not reality. It's normal that they are going to create something. They didn't create a lot - some actions, some mistakes from us. But I think it's normal."

Analysis: Man City continue to play with fire

Enzo Maresca has a point. You can't turn your nose up at winning away at FC Porto - an intimidating atmosphere, one that is not used to suffering defeat. Doing so in a manner where they conceded little in terms of clear chances is also a positive.

But look at City's performances this season. Trounced in the Community Shield by Arsenal, then a late show to overcome Bournemouth with a fortunate win. Then came a resounding win over Crystal Palace, but then they nearly dropped the ball in their 1-0 win over Coventry.

This was another game where they could have dropped the ball. City dominated for 47 minutes but then allowed FC Porto back into it. There were slack passes and constant losses of possession - a better team would have found a way back into the game.

And City face a better test on Sunday. No team will be more desperate to take advantage of such play than Manchester United at Old Trafford. It will be another big atmosphere for Maresca's City to overcome. But if they continue to play with fire, they will get burnt.

Sports.title: Christie nets hat-trick as Bournemouth blitz Championship Lincoln
Sports.content:
Ryan Christie scored a hat-trick to give Marco Rose his first win as Bournemouth manager as the Cherries swept aside Sky Bet Championship side Lincoln 4-0.

The Scotland international starred for the hosts with goals in the seventh, 69th and 88th minutes for his second career hat-trick, with Rayan stepping off the bench to wrap up the Carabao Cup third-round victory in stoppage time.

Rose made eight changes, including handing a debut to on-loan Juventus goalkeeper Michele Di Gregorio and a first start for Uruguayan striker Alvaro Rodriguez.

Only Ryley Towler kept his place from Lincoln's 1-1 draw at home to Southampton as the two sides met for the first time since 2010 when they were both in League Two.

Lincoln started brightly, but it was Bournemouth who opened the scoring after just seven minutes when Christie finished neatly at the near post from Ben Gannon-Doak's cross.

The lively Gannon-Doak then saw his effort blocked by Towler after cutting in from the left wing and firing a right-footed shot.

Di Gregorio was called into action for the first time after 22 minutes, keeping out Dan Oyegoke's flick before Towler blazed over from the rebound.

Lincoln goalkeeper Joe Gauci made a smart save to deny Bafode Diakite after the defender had headed a long throw goalwards.

Image: Rayan scored a 94th-minute fourth goal for the hosts

James Hill then fired over from distance as Bournemouth went hunting for a second goal. Six minutes before half-time Cherries left-back Julio Soler curled wide from 25 yards after David Brooks' corner had been only half cleared.

Hill also saw a shot from the edge of the penalty area deflected behind for a corner, before Christie's curling 20-yard effort was palmed away by Gauci with the final kick of the first half.

Rose will be frustrated to have picked up just two points from his first three Premier League games after conceding late goals against Manchester City, Everton and Newcastle.

His side almost doubled their lead five minutes into the second half when Gannon-Doak's curling effort glanced off the head of Rodriguez and flew just over the crossbar.

Scotland international Gannon-Doak then ballooned another long-range effort over in the 55th minute.

Hill came close to picking out the top corner with a 25-yard piledriver which smacked against the angle of post and crossbar.

Rodriguez had another good chance to open his Bournemouth account moments later, but slipped as he lined up a shot from the edge of the box and sent it high into the stands.

The £21m signing later headed inches wide from Hill's cross as he endured a frustrating full debut.

Christie showed Rodriguez the route to goal 21 minutes from time by heading in Brooks' corner at the far post.

The Scotland midfielder completed his treble in the 88th minute with a deflected shot from 14 yards out after being teed up by Diakite.

Rayan made it 4-0 in stoppage time with a tidy finish from the corner of the six-yard box.

Sports.title: Southampton knock Swansea off Championship top spot
Sports.content:
Cyle Larin scored his fifth goal of the season as Southampton beat Swansea 3-1 to humble a table-topper for the second home match in a row.

Larin, who is the joint-top scorer in the Championship, netted either side of Finn Azaz and Leo Scienza strikes to make it 13 games unbeaten at St Mary's in a row.

It followed Saints hammering previous leaders Millwall 5-1 10 days ago, although Swansea - who netted through Zan Vipotnik's penalty - stayed level on points at the summit.

Image: Leo Scienza scored Southampton's third against Swansea

Swansea made five changes from the side which drew with Wrexham at the weekend and failed to have a shot on target in the first half - with the majority of their efforts blocked long before reaching Daniel Peretz.

On the other hand, the hosts were rampant as they eased through the Swans' lines.

Scienza and Ryan Manning were the first to find open spaces behind their opposition in the fourth minute, but after their neat interchange, Azaz skied high into the stand.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Southampton are in front against league leaders Swansea thanks to a lovely finish from Finn Azaz.

But five minutes later the Republic of Ireland international found the bottom corner with a low left-footed shot, after Flynn Downes had powered through.

It was Azaz's first goal in seven attempts against Swansea, his second of the season, and just the second goal the Swans had conceded in 2026-27.

Larin was the second player to go from putting supporters in the Chapel Stand at risk before scoring.

The Canadian snatched at a half-volley after a corner in the 25th minute, before sliding home eight minutes later.

This time James Bree had made the run in behind the porous defence before squaring to Larin for his fifth league strike of the campaign, after two blanks.

Midfielder Downes had an opportunity to completely put the game to bed two minutes before the interval but he hooked over the crossbar after a Larin knockdown.

Swansea boss Vitor Matos sent winger Ronald on at half-time and he brought immediate energy by bundling a shot over.

It was contagious for the away side, and within 10 minutes of the restart they had pulled a goal back.

Bree pulled back Vipotnik at the back post before the Slovenian picked himself up to fire into the bottom left corner from the spot - his seventh straight penalty success.

Despite a far more even balance of play, Southampton still had the better chances, as Keven Schlotterbeck's poke forced a good save and Larin's improvised header bounced narrowly wide.

And Scienza - who had seen a lashed shot battered away - secured the three points 12 minutes from the end by calmly slotting into the corner after being released by Kuryu Matsuki.

Sports.title: Colwill earns Cardiff point but winless start continues
Sports.content:
Cardiff's winless start to the season continued as Stoke held on for a 1-1 draw and their first away point since January in the Welsh capital.

Stoke had hope of an away-day success after a run of nine straight Sky Bet Championship defeats when Ben Johnson scored midway through the first half.

But the Potters came under fierce pressure in the second half and Joel Colwill's headed home for Cardiff hosts who hit a post three times.

Image: Joel Colwill scored Cardiff's equaliser against Stoke

The draw - Cardiff's fourth in six games - was enough to take the Bluebirds out of the relegation zone, while Stoke slip to 15th.

Krystian Bielik was named in the Cardiff starting line-up after being involved in a physical altercation with a fan at Portsmouth on Saturday.

The incident is currently the subject of an investigation by Hampshire Police.

Cardiff boss Brian Barry-Murphy had urged supporters and players to stay calm after a tricky start and two successive defeats that had dropped them into the relegation zone.

Stoke had been boosted by back-to-back home wins but their form on the road was dire, with no wins in 11 games.

Ollie Tanner had two chances in the space of 60 seconds for the Bluebirds.

A slick interchange of passes between Tanner, Jack Moylan and Yousef Salech allowed the winger space and his shot from 20 yards struck the base of a post.

Stoke escaped again immediately as goalkeeper Viktor Johansson, under pressure from Salech, sent his clearing kick straight to Tanner, who failed to find an empty net from a tight angle.

Robert Bozenik skewed Stoke's first opening wide, but the Potters were ahead after Tanner failed to convert at the far post.

Bozenik played the ball over the top of the Cardiff defence and Johnson profited from some weak defending to open his account on a season-long loan from Ipswich.

George Hirst forced Nathan Trott to shovel his effort from 20 yards, and the Cardiff goalkeeper had to react again to hold Justin Devenny's deflected shot.

Good chances came thick and fast at the start of the second half after Moylan fired straight at Johansson.

Hirst was clean through but he lacked conviction approaching Trott and the goalkeeper saved with his legs.

Tanner then burst away after dispossessing Luke Graham, but Ben Wilmot came to Stoke's rescue with a brilliant block that earned him high-fives all round.

Colwill met Chris Willock's cross after 63 minutes to broke Stoke's resistance, looping a header on to a post and past Johansson.

The same combination almost paid dividends for Cardiff moments later when another Colwill header thumped off a post.

Salech had two clear-cut chances late on and Moylan struck the goal frame in stoppage time as Cardiff were frustrated.

Sports.title: Burnley still without a win after draw at Wrexham
Sports.content:
Wrexham's wait for a home win goes on after they were held to a 1-1 draw by winless Burnley who sit one place off the bottom of the Sky Bet Championship.

Jacques Ekomie headed in his second goal for the club since joining in a £7million deal from Angers this summer, cancelling out Zeki Amdouni's first-half effort for the Clarets who at least ended a run of seven straight away defeats dating back to last term.

But it was a result that does little to help either side in their pursuit of promotion, with Wrexham having lost the momentum they carried into last season while Burnley have bigger problems following relegation from the top flight, having won only one league game since October.

Image: Burnley are still waiting for their first Championship win of the season

Former England striker Jamie Vardy joined this week, signing as a free agent after last season's top-scorer Zian Flemming was sold to Ipswich on deadline day, but the 39-year-old was suspended for this match as a result of yellow cards collected during his time with Italian side Cremonese.

He watched on as Wrexham should have led just four minutes in, when Callum Doyle headed straight at Max Weiss when Max Cleworth put Issa Kabore's cross back into the danger zone.

Moore went closest for the hosts in the 18th minute, seeing his close-range header well saved by Weiss after Doyle squared from Matty James' cross.

Burnley had created little but Largie Ramazani had been their brightest hope and the Leeds loanee provided the spark for the opening goal in the 26th minute, threading a perfect pass through for Amdouni to finish first time.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Merse lauds Jamie Vardy move as Burnley's signing arrives to watch Wrexham match as he is currently serving a match suspension.

The Swiss forward could have had a second moments later when his long-range strike deflected off Cleworth before Anthony Patterson stretched to push it wide.

Now it was Wrexham feeling the pressure with disquiet growing in the stands. A free-kick six minutes before the break gave them a chance to level but after James' low strike was well saved by Weiss, Kabore fired into the side-netting.

Wrexham went off to a smattering of boos at the break and Phil Parkinson responded by sending on deadline day signing Callum O'Hare for his home debut alongside Oli Rathbone.

Rathbone played a hand in Wrexham's equaliser but it was finished by the two wing-backs who signed on the same day last month, as Kabore's superb cross was met with a powerful header by Ekomie.

Wrexham tails were now up as O'Hare headed wide from James' cross. Kabore then picked off a short pass out from Weiss, but could not find a team-mate with his cross, then O'Hare flashed a shot wide after a defensive mix-up.

Burnley almost snatched a winner in the 73rd minute when Ekomie blocked Oliver Sonne's shot on the line, but it ended as another frustrating night for both sides.

Sports.title: Real Madrid cling on to beat Inter on Mourinho’s big Champions League night
Sports.content:
Sometimes football is silly and sometimes it is more fun for it. On a night when there were 37 shots and the goalkeepers shared thirteen saves between them, some of them absurd, José Mourinho’s Real Madrid found a way to beat his former team Inter in his first Champions League night of his second spell. Just don’t ask exactly how. Except perhaps to cite Thibaut Courtois, whose astonishing save in the 89th minute saw them hold on to a 2-0 first-half lead given then by goals from Kylian Mbappé and Fede Valverde themselves. You would say that they had shot themselves in the foot, only if they tried, Courtois would probably save that too. This wasn’t always good, in fact at times it was terrible, but they had got through somehow.

You would say that they had shot themselves in the foot, only if they tried, Courtois would probably save that too. This wasn’t always good, in fact at times it was terrible, but they had got through somehow. When Madrid scored the first, this grand arena cheered but they might as well have laughed too. That Madrid led really didn’t make much sense; not when it came to the goal and not when it came to the game either. It had taken Madrid four minutes to get a meaningful hold of the ball, and by then Courtois had already made a superb save from Marcus Thuram. But now, somehow, they led. Ninety minutes later, they still did.

Inter had been playing round them with what looked like an ease, until suddenly even the simplest things looked complicated. Hakan Calhanoglu had just fired off the third shot and Lautaro Martínez the fourth when it happened. Inter had enjoyed 65% of possession which actually felt like rather more until then suddenly gave it up, and in a way that was comic.

Under pressure from Trent Alexander-Arnold, Curtis Jones made a mess of the first ball, playing it back for Yann Bisseck who for one brief moment seemed to lose his bearing and his footing. Stumbling like someone had put his legs on the wrong way round, he gave it away to Brahim Díaz who first time sent Mbappé away and he finished past Josep Martínez. It was Madrid’s first shot, gifted their attack, and the opening goal.

Quick Guide Dortmund's Karetsas taken to hospital Show Borussia Dortmund's Konstantinos Karetsas was taken to hospital after slumping to the turf 25 minutes into his Champions League debut against Villarreal. “Konstantinos Karetsas had to leave the field due to circulatory problems,” Dortmund said in a statement. “Kosta is doing well under the circumstances and is on his way to the hospital for further tests.” The 18-year-old Greece international passed the ball to a teammate then signaled his distress to the referee before sitting on the grass. Karetsas was treated laying down then taken away on a stretcher. The score was 0-0 at the time. Dortmund went on to win 3-2 at home. Renato Veiga’s 53rd-minute own goal put the Bundesliga side ahead before Santiago Mouriño equalised in the 66th. Serhou Guirassy restored the lead in the 80th minute and scored the third with an 84th-minute penalty, before scoring an own goal in added time while trying to help in defence. Real Betis twice came from behind to beat Lille 3-2 away, ⁠with Marc Bartra scoring in the 34th and 49th minutes before Troy Parrott’s 54th-minute winner. Lille ​scored their opener in the 12th minute ‌and regained the lead through ‌Alexsandro in the 37th. The hosts later had Ethan Mbappé sent off for an elbow to ‌the face of an opponent. AEK Athens ​made a winning start, beating the Austrian side LASK 1-0 in Greece thanks to Romanian midfielder Razvan Marin’s curling free-kick midway through the first half. Agencies Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

If that was absurd, what came next was even more ridiculous. What is it that Real Madrid do to goalkeepers in this competition? Receiving on his line, Martínez saw Fede Valverde coming and tried a drag back, which of course failed. A swift flick of the ankle and from a metre, Valverde had scored. Twenty-three minutes had gone and it was 2-0.

The lead might even have grown when another awful loss saw Vinícius Júnior dashing away. This time, Bissek made a fantastic saving challenge right on the edge of the six-yard box. There was something exhilarating about Vinícius’s acceleration and for all the fortune this did start to feel a little like a plan now: force the mistake, punish it. Madrid would force many more too, which they didn’t punish. Inter, meanwhile, recovered and reasserted themselves, a calmness in possession at the top of the pitch that contrasted with the calamitousness in possession further back.

View image in fullscreen Kylian Mbappé opens the scoring for Real Madrid in the 14th minute. Photograph: Violeta Santos Moura/Reuters

Jones, Martínez and Carlos Augusto played their way round Madrid again, virtually walking into the area, Jones turning and smashing a shot off the bar. Then just before the break, another gift, this time from Benjamin Pavard, saw Madrid escape again. Mbappé got in, Bellingham was denied by a wonderful stop from Martínez and Díaz hit the post from the rebound. Inter led 12-3 in shots and had 70% of the ball. They had also completed 125 passes in the final third; Madrid had completed 13.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The second half began with Martínez coming out to stop Mbappé, dashing through again, but Inter came back at them. Madrid’s midfield just didn’t exist. Which didn’t always matter as they ran through it. Courtois, though, does: he saved from Jones. There was a Nicolò Barella shot wide and Thuram scooped over. Then the stadium then stood to applaud when Courtois made an outrageous double stop on 55 minutes which, although the flag was up anyway, spoke of a kind of disbelief.

The feeling was similar when Martínez saved Inter at the other end, somehow scrambling across his line to stop Jude Bellingham after Díaz’s glorious scoop over him and into the Englishman, three yards out. A competition was building between the goalkeepers. Inter, chasing, were increasingly open. Madrid could have killed this, and quite a few times. Equally, Inter could have opened it. On the hour Courtois saved from Alessandro Bastoni. At the other end, Martínez saved from Mbappé with his legs. That was 6-5 to Courtois.

There were some whistles, frustration appearing, but there was also a kind of wild fun about this now, the chances too quick to keep up with: the twenty seconds or so between Martínez getting blocked at one end and Díaz slotting wide at the other told a tale. Then a Valverde shot wiped out Bissek, bravely putting his head in the way of a thumping shot. Still Inter came, and they finally found their way through, another clean, incisive exchange finding Lautaro Martínez on the byline, from where he pulled back perfectly for Augusto to finish from six yard. There were fifteen minutes left and a game on, but that, somehow, was that.

Sports.title: Haaland double gives Manchester City ideal Champions League start in Porto
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca admitted a liking for the “boom-boom” of house music, then oversaw a gritty performance that ended with Manchester City enjoying the sweet notes of victory.

They had lost six of their past nine away games in the competition and also lost the 2021 Champions League final at this venue, so to beat Porto and claim three points is a fillip for the manager’s nascent project.

Factor in, too, how City face Paris Saint-Germain on matchday No 2, and travel to Manchester United for Sunday’s derby, and Maresca can be exuberant at his start as Pep Guardiola’s successor.

All four games have been won – maybe more than even he would have hoped for, Erling Haaland’s double keeping the perfect start going. With 16 points the accepted target to qualify automatically for the knockout stage, as this was required in the first two years of this format, Maresca may have considered a win here vital particularly as targeting four victories from City’s four home matches as necessary to reach the tally might founder due to the visit of the double European champions next month.

Maresca stood down Elliot Anderson and gave Ayyoub Bouaddi a full debut, alongside Enzo Fernández in midfield. Haaland was not given the rest Maresca stated he will need at some point soon, as the No 9 headed an attack that contained Phil Foden, Rayan Cherki and Antoine Semenyo behind.

Bouaddi, playing deeper than Fernández, proved calm, though a surge forward was followed by the Argentinian heading in the area.

The issue was Porto being content to allow City to pitter-patter passes about their backline and middle third and there being no quickness of play or penetration. Francesco Farioli’s men offered an example of exactly how when Marc Guéhi’s ball short-changed Bouaddi, possession was nabbed, and suddenly William Gomes had to be stopped on the edge of City’s area. Earlier, Gabriel Veiga sliced through the rearguard and had Gianluigi Donnarumma saving: the offside flag went up but here were two warnings.

Quick Guide Dortmund's Karetsas taken to hospital Show Borussia Dortmund's Konstantinos Karetsas was taken to hospital after slumping to the turf 25 minutes into his Champions League debut against Villarreal. “Konstantinos Karetsas had to leave the field due to circulatory problems,” Dortmund said in a statement. “Kosta is doing well under the circumstances and is on his way to the hospital for further tests.” The 18-year-old Greece international passed the ball to a teammate then signaled his distress to the referee before sitting on the grass. Karetsas was treated laying down then taken away on a stretcher. The score was 0-0 at the time. Dortmund went on to win 3-2 at home. Renato Veiga’s 53rd-minute own goal put the Bundesliga side ahead before Santiago Mouriño equalised in the 66th. Serhou Guirassy restored the lead in the 80th minute and scored the third with an 84th-minute penalty, before scoring an own goal in added time while trying to help in defence. Real Betis twice came from behind to beat Lille 3-2 away, ⁠with Marc Bartra scoring in the 34th and 49th minutes before Troy Parrott’s 54th-minute winner. Lille ​scored their opener in the 12th minute ‌and regained the lead through ‌Alexsandro in the 37th. The hosts later had Ethan Mbappé sent off for an elbow to ‌the face of an opponent. AEK Athens ​made a winning start, beating the Austrian side LASK 1-0 in Greece thanks to Romanian midfielder Razvan Marin’s curling free-kick midway through the first half. Agencies Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Discard the ponderous pace might have been Maresca’s message because when Foden switched flanks from the right and accelerated, Porto were splayed, and Haaland’s header from the cross required Diogo Costa’s gloves to keep the contest goalless.

A near-carbon copy came when Semenyo popped the ball over from the left but this time Haaland’s header sailed over. City were warming up: Foden, Cherki and Haaland all being denied, as Porto were caught in a chokehold in and around their area.

View image in fullscreen Erling Haaland outjumps Jakub Kiwior to head City into the lead. Photograph: Clive Brunskill/Getty Images

At Leicester and then Chelsea Maresca could draw criticism for a quasi-sideways style at times. Yet after the slowish passage, tonight’s XI had become direct and a threat, as when Bouaddi chipped the ball left from near halfway, it went forward at speed, and a panicked Porto cleared.

When Veiga went down after a challenge with Guéhi the match was halted, tempers frayed. The No 10 recovered – it appeared to be a head problem – and the action, finally, restarted before Szymon Marciniak blew his whistle for the break.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

After the now seemingly de rigueur fireworks before every Champions League game, Porto had begun with confidence sky-high after winning all five Primeira Liga outings so far and, when wandering off for half-time, they remained content.

The mood changed almost instantaneously. City, at last, showed the ruthlessness needed at this level. Cherki, breaking into the area, swerved left, leaving Costa stranded. He fed Fernández and Haaland headed his cross into the turf and home – the visitors had a priceless lead.

What would be Porto’s response? To rove upfield and go close to the equaliser, was the answer. Maresca’s team can be open, as they were when André Silva had an age to dip right and let fly, the former Portugal forward’s attempt hitting the side-netting.

The lead was slender, as it was in Saturday’s 1-0 win over Coventry. Maresca acted as the hour passed, removing Cherki and Semenyo for Elliot Anderson and Iliman Ndiaye: two attackers for one forward and a holding player in Anderson whose role was to try and exert control for City, and aid Bouaddi in snuffing out any Porto threat.

A second goal would also stymie the hosts, so Ndiaye skipped across the grass, and unloaded, though the effort went straight into Costa’s clutches. Foden, too, tried to break in behind but the ball was shepherded back to the Porto keeper.

Whenever Farioli’s team moved forward City remained vulnerable despite Anderson’s presence. By the close, though, Haaland’s late right-foot stab ensured the result, and meant that even an interval dispute in the tunnel due to the Veiga-Guéhi clash was of scant import to City, despite tempers again meaning a further row.

Sports.title: First-half treble powers Aston Villa to Champions League win at Club Brugge
Sports.content:
Aston Villa were 3-1 up after 43 minutes but were made to sweat for their first win of the season, emerging victorious from an entertaining Champions League opener with Club Brugge. John McGinn, who struck the only goal when Villa belatedly got their season up and running last September against Bologna, opened the scoring before Emi Buendía and a first goal for Nicolas Jackson in claret and blue appeared to put Villa out of sight at half-time.

The Belgian side have become familiar foes since Villa returned to the big time, the glitziest club competition of them all; a freakish Tyrone Mings handball gifted the hosts a penalty, and subsequently victory, in 2024-25 and on this occasion Aaron Wan-Bissaka conceded a second-half penalty to plunge a seesawing contest back into the balance.

“Today was a very important step forward, being resilient when we were struggling,” said Unai Emery. “It is very important to start with three points. Hopefully it gives us confidence for the next matches, in the Premier League this Saturday against Nottingham Forest.”

Emery had been at pains to radiate positivity despite another slow start – Villa picked up their first point of the Premier League season at the weekend and these goals represented their first of the campaign – but he was typically animated on the touchline in Brugge. He was particularly agitated midway through the second half when he felt, not for the first time this season, his substitutes were not ready for action. At Hull last weekend, it was Tammy Abraham and Wan-Bissaka, and a few days earlier Alejandro Garnacho against Arsenal.

This time the culprits were Alysson, Ross Barkley and Lamare Bogarde. “In the dressing room at half-time we were speaking about some players who were tired, [Boubacar] Kamara, Wan-Bissaka,” Villa’s manager said. “I tried to keep [them on for] 15 minutes, but when I asked the players to replace [them] they were talking through the set pieces, sorting individual issues, but I needed quickly their impact on the field, and they did afterwards.”

In the end, it was a blend of old and new faces that got Villa over the line. Zion Suzuki made a couple of fine saves, João Gomes put in a typically tigerish performance and Jackson got the goal an encouraging all-round display deserved. The 19-year-old George Hemmings did not look out of place on his Champions League debut. “The old players need to keep our standards high, to show everybody this is the only way we can achieve the process in our objectives and targets,” Emery said. “I am so happy.”

Pau Torres was the unlikely catalyst for two of Villa’s three first-half goals. McGinn’s opener was a product of the centre-back roaming unchallenged to the edge of the box. Presumably it crossed Torres’s mind to shoot, though just as he was getting giddy, he spread play to McGinn, who guided a superb first-time, left-foot strike into the far corner of Yann Sommer’s goal. In starting on Tuesday night, the Swiss became just the second goalkeeper to represent five clubs in the Champions League, but it was a night to forget for the 37-year-old.

View image in fullscreen John McGinn punches the air after giving Aston Villa an 11th-minute lead. Photograph: PA Wire/PA

Club Brugge replied when the lively Jan Virgili found a way past Wan-Bissaka – who was making his full Villa debut – and located Hugo Vetlesen in the box, the Norway midfielder sending a crisp finish beyond Suzuki. The hosts were level for less than three minutes, a slick Villa move culminating in Buendía wheeling away in celebration. Jackson’s deft backheel supplied Gomes, who twisted inside the box and then picked out Buendía who did the rest.
